examples.en: Housekeepers often appear in old dramas.

examples.ko: 그 부잣집에는 가정부 두 명이 일해요.
examples.en: Two housekeepers work in that wealthy household.
I saw an advertisement looking for a housekeeper.

examples.ko: 영화 속 가정부는 사실 비밀을 알고 있었어요.
examples.en: The housekeeper in the movie actually knew a secret.
A housekeeper who came from abroad helps with the housework.
Thanks to the housekeeper, the house is always clean.

explain: 요즘 일상에서는 '가정부'보다 '가사도우미', '도우미 아주머니'라고 더 많이 말해요. 가정부는 드라마나 영화에서 자주 들리는 오래된 느낌의 말이에요. 직접 부를 때는 '이모님'처럼 존중하는 호칭을 써요.
explain_en: In daily life people now more often say 가사도우미 or 도우미 아주머니 than 가정부. 가정부 sounds a bit old-fashioned and shows up mostly in dramas and movies. When speaking to the person directly, a respectful title like 이모님 is used.

examples.en: That comedian's facial expressions are really funny.
When I was little, my dream was to be a comedian.
The comedian sang a song on the broadcast.

examples.ko: 저는 개그우먼 한 분을 아주 좋아해요.
examples.en: I really like one of the comedians.
I took a photo with my comedian friend.
People lined up to see the comedian.

explain: 남자는 '개그맨', 여자는 '개그우먼'이라고 해요. 성별 없이 부를 때는 '코미디언'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: A male one is a 개그맨 and a female one is a 개그우먼. To refer to either without gender, people also say 코미디언.

examples.en: This school has an excellent faculty.

examples.ko: 새 학기에 교수진이 몇 명 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: A few members of the faculty changed this semester.

examples.ko: 학교 홈페이지에서 교수진 소개를 읽어 봤어요.
examples.en: I read the faculty introduction on the school website.

examples.ko: 외국인 교수진이 많은 학교를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a school with many foreign faculty.
The faculty and students had lunch together.
The department faculty's research fields are varied.

explain: 교수진은 한 학교나 학과의 교수들을 한꺼번에 가리키는 말이라 한 사람에게는 쓰지 않아요. 그 사람은 '교수님'이라고 불러요. 학원이나 병원처럼 가르치거나 치료하는 사람들의 팀은 '강사진', '의료진'처럼 '-진'을 붙여요.
explain_en: 교수진 refers to all professors of a school or department together, so you don't use it for one person, who is addressed as '교수님'. The suffix '-진' also makes words for other groups, such as '강사진' (instructors) and '의료진' (medical staff).

examples.en: I get along well with my classmates.
I finished my homework with a classmate's help.

examples.ko: 급우 중에 노래를 잘하는 친구가 있어요.
examples.en: Among my classmates, there is a friend who sings well.
I quickly became close with my new classmate.

examples.ko: 급우 한 명이 전학을 가서 아쉬워요.
examples.en: One classmate transferred to another school, which is a pity.
The teacher told us to help our classmates.

explain: 같은 반 친구를 뜻하지만 글이나 공식적인 말에서 주로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '반 친구'라고 말하는 게 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It means a classmate but is mostly used in writing or formal speech. In everyday conversation, '반 친구' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 우리 담임 선생님은 다정다감해서 학생들이 좋아해요.
examples.en: Our homeroom teacher is warm and tender, so the students like her.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 겉으로는 무뚝뚝해도 속은 다정다감해요.
examples.en: He looks gruff on the outside, but he's tender inside.

examples.ko: 다정다감한 아버지 덕분에 저는 편하게 자랐어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my tender-hearted father, I grew up comfortably.

examples.ko: 남편이 다정다감하게 안부를 물어 줘서 고마웠어요.
examples.en: I was grateful that my husband asked after me so warmly.
When I was little, my grandmother was always warm and tender.
I'm not a tender person, so I'm clumsy at showing feelings.

explain: '다정하다'와 비슷한데, 마음이 따뜻할 뿐 아니라 감정이 풍부하고 정이 많은 사람에게 써요. 주로 사람의 성격을 말할 때 나와요. 반대로는 '무뚝뚝하다'를 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is close to '다정하다', but it describes someone who is not only kind but also rich in feeling and affection. It is mostly used for a person's character. A common opposite is '무뚝뚝하다'.

examples.en: I decided to go to the high school alumni meeting tomorrow.
I met my seniors after a long time at the alumni meeting.

examples.ko: 동문회 회장님이 모임 장소를 정해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The president of the alumni association chose the meeting place.
Our school's alumni association collected scholarship money.
The alumni meeting is held every autumn.
I was introduced to a good job through the alumni association.

explain: 같은 학교를 졸업한 사람들의 모임이에요. '동창회'는 같은 해에 졸업한 친구들의 모임으로 많이 쓰고, 동문회는 선배와 후배까지 같은 학교 출신이 모두 모이는 모임으로 많이 써요. '서울대 동문회'처럼 학교 이름을 앞에 붙여요.
explain_en: It is a gathering of people who graduated from the same school. 동창회 is mostly used for friends who graduated the same year, while 동문회 is mostly used for everyone from the same school, including seniors and juniors. The school name goes in front, like '서울대 동문회'.

examples.ko: 자동차 딜러가 차 종류를 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: The car dealer explained the types of cars.
I met a dealer because I wanted to buy a new car.
I asked the dealer to lower the price.

examples.ko: 외환 딜러는 하루 종일 화면을 봐요.
examples.en: A foreign exchange dealer watches the screen all day.
I signed the car contract after talking with the dealer.
I have a friend who works as a dealer.

explain: 딜러는 앞에 말을 붙여서 어떤 일을 하는지 말해요. '자동차 딜러', '외환 딜러'처럼요. 물건이 아니라 사람을 가리키는 말이에요.
explain_en: 딜러 takes a word in front to say what the person deals in, as in '자동차 딜러' and '외환 딜러'. It refers to a person, not a thing.

examples.en: An Olympic medalist came to our school to give a talk.
That athlete is a medalist at a world championship.
The three medalists stepped onto the podium.

examples.ko: 저는 메달리스트를 꿈꾸며 매일 새벽에 훈련해요.
examples.en: I train every dawn, dreaming of becoming a medalist.
I saw a medalist's interview on the news yesterday.
There is prize money for the medalists of this competition.

explain: '금메달리스트', '은메달리스트', '동메달리스트'처럼 앞에 색을 붙여 써요. 메달을 땄다는 말은 '메달을 따다'라고 해요. 뉴스와 스포츠 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: You can put the color in front, as in '금메달리스트', '은메달리스트' and '동메달리스트'. Winning a medal is said '메달을 따다'. It often appears in news and sports talk.

examples.en: I walked slowly out of consideration for my friend.
If we are considerate of each other, there is nothing to fight about.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 늘 다른 사람을 배려하는 편이에요.
examples.en: That person tends to always think of others.
It was a considerate thing to say, so it felt good.

examples.ko: 아이를 배려하지 않은 행동에 화가 났어요.
examples.en: I was angry at the behavior that showed no thought for the child.
I will be more considerate from now on.

explain: 명사로는 '배려가 깊다', '배려심이 있다'처럼 써요. '신경 쓰다'는 더 가볍게 쓰고, '배려하다'는 상대 입장을 생각해서 행동한다는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: The noun appears in '배려가 깊다' (very considerate) and '배려심이 있다' (have a considerate heart). '신경 쓰다' (pay attention) is lighter, while '배려하다' suggests acting from the other person's point of view.

examples.en: The child grew up under his grandmother's care.

examples.ko: 이 아기 고양이는 보살핌이 많이 필요해요.
examples.en: This kitten needs a lot of care.
I was grateful to receive warm care at the hospital.
Even a potted plant withers quickly without care.
For older people, family care and attention are important.
Thanks to my parents' care, I became healthy.

explain: '돌봄'은 돌보는 일 자체를 말하고, 보살핌은 받는 쪽에서 더 자주 써요. '보살핌을 받다', '보살핌이 필요하다'가 자연스러워요. 하는 쪽은 '보살피다', '돌보다'로 말해요.
explain_en: 돌봄 names the act of caring itself, while 보살핌 is used more from the side of the person being cared for. 보살핌을 받다 and 보살핌이 필요하다 sound natural. The person giving care says 보살피다 or 돌보다.

examples.en: I'm a freshman at university this year.
I met the seniors at the freshman welcome party.

examples.ko: 회사에 들어온 새내기 직원이 열심히 배우고 있어요.
examples.en: The new employee who joined the company is learning hard.
When I was a freshman, everything felt new and exciting.

examples.ko: 새내기들은 아직 학교 건물을 잘 몰라요.
examples.en: The freshmen don't know the school buildings well yet.
The political newcomer gave his first speech.

explain: 새로 들어온 사람, 특히 대학 1학년을 친근하게 부르는 말이에요. 순우리말이라 느낌이 부드럽고, 같은 뜻의 '신입생'은 학교가 정한 공식적인 말이에요. 회사에서는 '신입 사원'이라고 하고 '새내기'는 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: 새내기 is a friendly word for someone new, especially a first-year university student. It is a native Korean word with a soft feel, whereas 신입생 is the official term. At work the formal term is 신입 사원, with 새내기 used more lightly.

examples.en: The captain docked the big ship at the port.
When the storm came, the captain called everyone.
When I was little, I dreamed of being a ship captain.
I greeted the captain and boarded the ship.

examples.ko: 이 배의 선장과 이야기해 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to talk with the captain of this ship.

examples.ko: 오랜 경력의 선장에게 바다 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard sea stories from a veteran captain.

explain: 배의 책임자예요. 비행기의 책임자는 '기장', 군함의 지휘관은 '함장'이라고 불러요. 높여 부를 때는 '선장님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: The person in charge of a ship. The person in charge of a plane is '기장', and a warship commander is '함장'. To address one politely, say '선장님'.

examples.en: The newborn sleeps all day long.
My sister held a newborn for the first time.

examples.ko: 병원에는 신생아 전용 방이 따로 있어요.
examples.en: The hospital has a separate room just for newborns.
Newborns need a quiet environment.

examples.ko: 어제 우리 동네에서 신생아 세 명이 태어났대요.
examples.en: I heard three newborns were born in our neighborhood yesterday.
Newborn clothes are very small and soft.

explain: 갓 태어난 아기를 말할 때 '신생아'는 병원이나 뉴스처럼 조금 공식적인 자리에서 많이 써요. 가족끼리는 그냥 '아기'라고 하고, '갓난아기'는 더 부드럽고 친근하게 들려요.
explain_en: 신생아 is the word you hear in hospitals and the news for a baby just born. Within the family people just say '아기', and '갓난아기' sounds softer and warmer.

examples.ko: 앞사람 머리 때문에 영화 화면이 안 보여요.
examples.en: I can't see the movie screen because of the head of the person in front of me.
The person ahead stopped suddenly and I almost bumped into them.

examples.ko: 줄을 설 때는 앞사람과 거리를 두세요.
examples.en: When standing in line, keep some distance from the person in front.
I followed the person ahead and walked in slowly.
After the person ahead got off, I sat down.
When the person before me finishes talking, I'll ask my question too.

explain: 줄이나 자리, 순서에서 바로 앞에 있는 사람을 말하고, 반대말은 '뒷사람'이에요. 보통 줄 서기, 극장 좌석, 발표 순서 같은 상황에서 써요.
explain_en: It means the person right in front of you in a line, seat or order, and the opposite is '뒷사람'. It typically comes up in situations like queuing, theater seats and speaking order.

examples.en: The heroine of this drama is a brave nurse.

examples.ko: 여주인공이 눈물을 흘리는 장면에서 저도 울었어요.
examples.en: I cried too in the scene where the heroine sheds tears.

examples.ko: 새 영화에서 유명한 배우가 여주인공을 맡았어요.
examples.en: A famous actress took the female lead in the new movie.
I was drawn to the heroine of the novel.

examples.ko: 여주인공과 남자 주인공이 처음 만나는 장면이 재미있어요.
examples.en: The scene where the heroine and hero first meet is fun.

examples.ko: 저는 여주인공 역할을 꼭 해 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I really want to try playing the female lead.

explain: 이야기에서 중심이 되는 여자 인물이에요. 남자는 '남자 주인공'이라고 하고, 성별 구분 없이는 그냥 '주인공'이라고 해요.
explain_en: This is the central female character in a story. The male counterpart is 남자 주인공, and the plain word 주인공 works with no gender.

examples.ko: 할머니는 외손자가 오는 날을 손꼽아 기다리세요.
examples.en: Grandmother counts the days until her grandson visits.
Our grandson has already become an elementary school student.

examples.ko: 외손자에게 용돈을 주고 싶어서 은행에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the bank because I wanted to give my grandson some pocket money.

examples.ko: 할아버지께서 외손자 이름을 직접 지어 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandfather named his grandson himself.
He is a person who cherishes his daughter's son and his son's son equally.

examples.ko: 마을 어른들께 외할아버지 성함을 말하며 외손자라고 인사드렸어요.
examples.en: I greeted the village elders by saying my maternal grandfather's name and that I was his grandson.

explain: 아들 쪽 손자는 '친손자'라고 구별해요. 손녀는 '외손녀'예요. 앞에서 부를 때는 보통 이름으로 부르고, '외손자'는 남에게 소개하거나 이야기할 때 써요.
explain_en: A grandson on the son's side is called '친손자', to tell them apart. A granddaughter is '외손녀'. To their face people usually call them by name; '외손자' is used when introducing or talking about them.

examples.en: Our teacher's classes are always humorous.

examples.ko: 유머러스한 사람과 있으면 시간이 빨리 가요.
examples.en: Time goes by fast when I'm with a humorous person.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 인터뷰도 유머러스하게 해서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: That actor does his interviews humorously too, so he is popular.
The content was funny, so I laughed while reading the book.

examples.ko: 저는 유머러스하지 않아서 농담을 잘 못해요.
examples.en: I'm not humorous, so I'm bad at making jokes.
If you start a presentation humorously, the mood gets better.

explain: 사람의 말이나 글, 분위기가 웃음을 주는 좋은 느낌일 때 써요. 그냥 '웃기다'는 상황이 우스울 때도 쓰지만, '유머러스하다'는 재치 있고 센스 있다는 칭찬에 가까워요. 외래어에서 온 말이라 '유머 감각이 있다'로 바꿔 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is used when someone's words, writing or mood is pleasantly funny. '웃기다' can describe any funny situation, while '유머러스하다' is closer to praising someone as witty. It comes from a loanword, and people also say '유머 감각이 있다' instead.

examples.en: My teacher is a benefactor of my life.

examples.ko: 어려울 때 도와준 은인을 잊지 못해요.
examples.en: I can't forget the benefactor who helped me in hard times.

examples.ko: 길에서 쓰러진 저를 구해 준 은인을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for the person who saved me when I collapsed on the street.
That person is a benefactor of our family.
I sent a small gift to my benefactor.
I cried when I met my benefactor.

explain: 큰 도움을 줘서 평생 고마워해야 하는 사람이에요. 가벼운 도움에는 '고마운 분'이라고 하고, '은인'은 정말 큰 은혜를 입었을 때 써요. 말할 때 자신을 낮추고 상대를 높이는 진지한 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: A person who helped you so greatly that you stay grateful for life. For a small favor Koreans say 고마운 분, and 은인 is reserved for a real debt of gratitude. It is a serious word that lifts the other person up.

examples.en: Both blood relatives and in-laws came to the wedding.
I often meet my relatives by marriage during the holidays.
I heard he is a distant in-law of the boss.

examples.ko: 서류에 인척 관계를 적는 칸이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a box on the form to write your in-law relationship.

examples.ko: 인척이 많아서 이름을 다 외우기 힘들어요.
examples.en: I have so many in-laws that it's hard to remember all the names.
They say the company doesn't hire relatives by marriage.

explain: '인척'은 결혼으로 가족이 된 친척이에요. 피로 이어진 친척은 '혈족'이라고 하고, 둘을 합쳐 '친척'이라고 말해요. 일상 대화보다 서류나 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: 인척 are relatives who became family through marriage. Blood relatives are called 혈족, and together both are 친척. You see 인척 more in documents and news than in daily conversation.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 재결합 소식에 팬들이 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Fans were surprised at the news of the two getting back together.

examples.ko: 그 가수들은 십 년 만에 재결합 공연을 해요.
examples.en: Those singers are doing a reunion concert after ten years.
A couple getting back together is not an easy decision.
When talk of a reunion came up, the mood turned awkward.
Many people are waiting for the band's reunion.

examples.ko: 회사를 나눈 뒤 재결합할 가능성은 낮아 보여요.
examples.en: After the company split, the chance of rejoining looks low.

explain: 헤어졌던 사람이나 집단이 다시 합치는 것이에요. 뉴스에서는 해체했던 그룹의 활동 재개, 헤어졌던 연인·부부가 다시 만나는 경우에 써요. 연인이 다시 만나는 것은 구어로 '다시 사귀다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is people or groups who had split coming together again. In the news it covers a disbanded group resuming activity or an ex-couple reuniting. In casual speech, a couple getting back together is 다시 사귀다.

examples.ko: 젖먹이를 안고 병원에 가는 엄마가 보였어요.
examples.en: I saw a mother carrying a nursing baby to the hospital.

examples.ko: 우리 집에는 젖먹이가 있어서 밤에 자주 깨요.
examples.en: We have a nursing baby at home, so I wake up often at night.

examples.ko: 젖먹이 때는 하루에도 몇 번씩 먹여야 해요.
examples.en: When they are nursing babies, you have to feed them several times a day.
Please dress the nursing baby in warm clothes.

examples.ko: 그 젖먹이도 이제 웃을 줄 알아요.
examples.en: That nursing baby can smile now too.

examples.ko: 동생이 젖먹이처럼 자꾸 안아 달라고 해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling keeps asking to be held like a little baby.

explain: 아직 젖이나 분유를 먹는 시기의 아기를 말해요. 일상에서는 그냥 '아기'라고 말해도 되고, '젖먹이'는 이야기나 글에서 아주 어린 아기를 강조할 때 어울려요. 태어난 지 얼마 안 된 아기는 '갓난아기'라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a baby who is still drinking milk or formula. In daily talk you can just say '아기', and '젖먹이' fits stories or writing that stress how very young the baby is. A newborn is called '갓난아기'.

examples.en: My friend's grandmother is coming this afternoon.
I have to write my grandmother's name on the form.

examples.ko: 조모와 함께 살았던 집이 아직 있어요.
examples.en: The house where I lived with my grandmother still exists.
I am going to see my grandmother this weekend.

examples.ko: 조모는 어릴 때 이야기를 자주 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother often told me stories from her childhood.
My grandmother will also attend the wedding.

explain: 평소에는 '할머니'라고 하고, 조모는 서류나 격식 있는 글에서 써요. 남의 할머니는 '조모님'이라고 높여요. 엄마 쪽 할머니는 '외조모'라고 해요.
explain_en: In daily life people say 할머니, and 조모 appears in documents and formal writing. Someone else's grandmother is the honorific '조모님'. A mother's mother is '외조모'.

examples.en: The whole nation cheered for the players with one heart.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 한마음이 되어 위기를 넘겼어요.
examples.en: Our team became of one mind and got through the crisis.

examples.ko: 한마음으로 노력하면 못 할 일이 없어요.
examples.en: If we work with one mind, there is nothing we can't do.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 한마음이라 말하지 않아도 잘 통해요.
examples.en: The two are of one mind, so they understand each other without words.

examples.ko: 반 친구들이 한마음으로 선생님께 선물을 준비했어요.
examples.en: The classmates prepared a gift for the teacher with one mind.

examples.ko: 한마음 한뜻으로 이 일을 꼭 해내요.
examples.en: With one heart and one will, let's get this done.

explain: 여러 사람이 같은 마음으로 뭉친다는 좋은 느낌이 있어요. '한마음으로', '한마음이 되다'처럼 자주 써요. 응원, 협력, 위기 극복 같은 상황에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It has a warm feel of many people uniting with the same heart. It is often used as '한마음으로' or '한마음이 되다'. It suits cheering, cooperation and overcoming a crisis.

examples.en: An environmental activist came to our school.
The activist collected signatures on the street.
I interviewed a human rights activist in person.
There is time to ask that activist questions.
We picked up beach trash together with an activist.
Young activists are also increasing.

explain: '환경 활동가', '인권 활동가'처럼 앞에 분야 이름을 붙여 자주 써요. 사회 문제를 바꾸려고 움직이는 사람에게 쓰기 때문에 일반 직업 이름과는 조금 달라요.
explain_en: It usually takes a field name in front, as in '환경 활동가' and '인권 활동가'. It is for people working to change social issues, so it feels a bit different from an ordinary job title.
